audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the full-layer chart disagreed with the content layer and the packet levelChart (full gave Zed level 1 and level 6, and 'Skill' where the other two say Zed at 4-5 and first item, Orianna at 2+ items).
audit.why: Packet and content agree with each other and with the kit: pre-6 Razor Shuriken costs 75 energy at rank 1 against her 815-range ball, so level 1 is hers; his first lethality item plus a 20s Living Shadow owns the roaming phase; grouped, a 410-range Shockwave and protect-ball beat a single-target assassin.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved onto the content/packet verdict on all five rows, with whys and ratings rewritten to match. win[] already held the correct tokens.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content whys were offset by a row: whys[2] described 'the level 6 tipping point' under the Level 3 label, and whys[3] claimed 'with R up Zed's all-in burst' under the Levels 4-5 label, where he has no ultimate at all.
audit.why: Death Mark is not available until level 6, so the Levels 4-5 row was telling the reader to fear an ability the enemy cannot cast.
audit.corrected: whys[1] to whys[4] rewritten onto their own rows using Razor Shuriken's 900 range, Living Shadow's 20s, Shadow Slash falling to 3.5s, and Death Mark's 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that no Zed ability is ever named on the full layer, and no interaction was stated.
audit.why: Death Mark makes him untargetable through the dash and pops 3 seconds after the mark, which is why Stopwatch is spent after the mark lands and not before. Living Shadow places a shadow up to 650 away and swaps him back to it — that swap point is what your R answers. Both his Q and your Q are projectiles.
audit.corrected: Names and numbers now carried in breakdown.cooldowns, the phase whys and every do's/don'ts body.

audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Death Mark 120s and its 3-second mark, Living Shadow 20s, Shadow Slash 5s->3s stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and dontsFull[0].d called a single male enemy 'they'.
audit.why: Lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED plus a pronoun defect — the owner is addressed as 'you', so the third person refers to Zed, who is male.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten; the shadow-return bullet now actually explains the shadow return.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.mid claimed protect-ball 'doubles every gank' (lint UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE).
audit.corrected: Replaced with what the ball actually delivers.

edits.after: Grouped you win: Shockwave and protect-ball swing the whole 5v5, while he can only pick a straggler off a flank.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Check it before every step-up. - E Command: Protect is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Death Mark (R): 120s at rank 1, with 3 seconds between the mark and the pop — spend Stopwatch after it lands, never before. - Living Shadow (W): 20s at rank 1, and with it down he cannot escape a gank. - Shadow Slash (E): 5s falling to 3s.

edits.before: From Luden's you run rivers: shove the wave, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first clump that contests. Protect-ball on your jungler doubles every gank.
edits.after: From Luden's you run rivers: shove, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first dive that commits. Protect-ball brings a shield, the speed field and your R to the gank.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: He is untargetable through the dash, so the ball sitting on you is what greets him when he lands, not your R.

edits.before: Ball on his farm path, Q-W the last-hit contact, auto-weave once, and recall the ball — three-second trades his combo math can't answer.
edits.after: Living Shadow swaps him back to a shadow he placed up to 650 away — put the R on that spot and the swap ends on your ball.

edits.before: Zed burns Death Mark on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Death Mark is 120s at rank 1, and a Stopwatch bought at 6 outlives every mark.

edits.before: That’s Zed’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Ball-less at 6 he marks you and there is no answer left but Flash.

edits.after: Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1 — while it is up your third combo is his gap-closer, so take two and step back.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Zed wins by marking you through your Stopwatch, swapping shadows out of your R, and roaming while you hold the wave.

edits.before: If Zed opens the score, reset expectations and respect Death Mark doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q-W clears and stay relevant through Shockwave threat.
edits.after: A kill funds his lethality and Death Mark starts killing outright, so hold Stopwatch for the mark and farm from behind minions. Two kills: never walk a sidelane alone and group where his pick threat dies.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry through the ball — protect-ball on whoever he marks blunts the repeated damage, and one Shockwave drags him off your carry.

edits.before: Skill — the early-to-mid transition trades hinge on execution: her poke vs his shadow-Q spacing.
edits.after: Skill — at 2 your Q-W chunk meets his 900-range shuriken; poke wins if you dodge the shadow line.

edits.before: Skill — around the level 6 tipping point it's about who uses cooldowns better before ults define the fight.
edits.after: Skill — at 3 your full combo meets his 20s Living Shadow, so the trade goes to whoever spends cooldowns better.

edits.before: Zed — with R up Zed's all-in burst (R + shadow Q + ignite) beats Orianna unless she perfectly times stasis.
edits.after: Zed — his Shadow Slash is down to 3.5s and shadow-Q poke chips her while mana runs the trade clock.

edits.before: Skill — the Zhonya's-vs-ult mindgame is an even read: bait vs commit is a coinflip of timing.
edits.after: Skill — Death Mark at 120s against her Stopwatch and 110s R: bait versus commit is a pure read.

notes: Five of seven full-layer chart rows disagreed with the content layer and the packet; the full layer was moved onto their shared verdict and win[] needed no edit. The content whys were also offset by a row — most seriously whys[3], which told the reader to fear 'R + shadow Q + ignite' on the Levels 4-5 row, where Zed has no ultimate; whys[1] to whys[4] now describe their own rows. dontsFull[0].d referred to Zed as 'they'. One thing I did not touch: the content chart itself gives Zed the Levels 4-5 row and 'Skill' at Level 6, which reads backwards for an assassin, but the packet levelChart says the same thing, so per the chart rule I left the tokens alone and only made the sentences under them true.
